nameStory: The crested blenny gets its name from the distinctive crest-like fin structure on its head, which stands up like a tiny mohawk hairstyle. This prominent feature makes it easy to spot among the rocky crevices where it lives, giving it a punk rock appearance that's hard to miss.
description: The crested blenny is a small, elongated fish that belongs to the combtooth blenny family. These little fish have a distinctive crest on their heads and typically grow to about 4 inches long. They're bottom-dwellers with a somewhat eel-like body shape, perfectly designed for squeezing into tight rocky spaces along the coast.

idTips.label: Body Shape
idTips.description: Long, slender body that feels smooth and slippery to the touch, with a somewhat compressed, eel-like appearance that tapers toward the tail

idTips.label: Fins
idTips.description: Prominent head crest formed by the dorsal fin, which feels firm and spiny when gently touched - this is their signature feature

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Small fish reaching about 4 inches maximum length, roughly the size of your index finger

idTips.label: Mouth
idTips.description: Small terminal mouth positioned at the front of the blunt head, with tiny comb-like teeth that give the family its name

idTips.label: Habitat
idTips.description: Found wedged in rocky crevices and tide pools where they feel secure against your fingers when gently coaxed

habitat: Crested blennies live in shallow coastal waters along rocky shores and tide pools throughout New England's coastline. They prefer areas with plenty of crevices and small caves in the intertidal zone where they can hide from predators. Look for them in protected rocky areas during low tide, especially around granite ledges and boulder fields.

seasonality.spring: Active in warming tide pools as water temperatures rise, beginning to establish territories among the rocks.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity period with spawning behavior visible in shallow rocky areas. Most likely time to spot them during tide pool exploration.
seasonality.fall: Still active but beginning to move to slightly deeper water as temperatures cool. Good time for observation before winter.
seasonality.winter: Less active and harder to find as they retreat to deeper crevices and slightly offshore areas for protection from storms.

funFact: Despite being only 4 inches long, crested blennies are incredibly territorial and will fearlessly charge at fish many times their size, using their head crest like a battle flag to intimidate intruders from their rocky homes.
confusionNotes: Most likely confused with other small tide pool fish like gobies, but the distinctive head crest is a dead giveaway - if you see a "mohawk," you've found a blenny. Remember: crest equals crested blenny.
contextualKnowledge: The term "combtooth" refers to their tiny, closely-spaced teeth that look like the teeth of a fine comb, though you'd need a magnifying glass to see this feature clearly. This family name is much more technical than what you'd actually use to identify them in the field.
compareHints: As the only Hypleurochilus species in New England waters, crested blennies are most similar to other blenny family members. However, their prominent head crest distinguishes them from other local blennies, which typically have more uniform dorsal fins. The crest feature is unique among New England's coastal fish fauna.
